winners.premise: A woman lends her favorite custom-made dress to a friend for one dinner, only to get it back permanently shortened and altered while the friend insists a dry cleaner ruined it by accident.
winners.conflict: The narrator's friend returns a borrowed custom dress with eight inches cut off the hem and several hand-sewn details removed, then refuses responsibility and blames an unnamed dry cleaner.
winners.twist: A forgotten alteration receipt in the dress pocket shows the friend personally requested the shorter hem and removal of the handmade details because she wanted the dress to suit her own style.
winners.hook: My friend borrowed my favorite dress for one dinner and returned it eight inches shorter.
winners.narration:
I made that dress with my aunt the summer after college. It wasn't expensive because of the fabric. It mattered because we spent three weekends fitting it, sewing tiny bead details by hand, and fixing every little mistake ourselves. So when my friend Mia asked to borrow it for an anniversary dinner, I hesitated. She promised she'd be careful, promised she'd wear it exactly once, and even joked that she'd guard it with her life.

Two days later she handed it back in a garment bag and left unusually fast. I opened it and thought I had the wrong dress. The hem was nearly eight inches shorter. The beaded trim my aunt had sewn around the sleeves was gone. Even the waist had been taken in.

I called Mia immediately. She sounded shocked for about three seconds, then said the dry cleaner must have damaged it. According to her, she had spilled sauce at dinner, sent the dress for emergency cleaning, and the shop had somehow decided to alter it without permission.

That explanation made no sense. Dry cleaners do not randomly redesign clothes. I asked for the shop name because I wanted to speak to them. Mia suddenly couldn't remember it. Then she said her boyfriend had dropped it off. Then she said maybe it was a tailoring service inside the cleaner and she wasn't sure.

While checking the pockets before storing the dress, I found a folded receipt. It listed the shop name, Mia's phone number, and four alteration requests: shorten hem eight inches, remove sleeve beading, taper waist, press for Friday pickup. At the bottom was her signature.

I sent her a photo of the receipt and asked one question: why?

She finally admitted she thought the dress looked 'dated' and wanted it to photograph better on her. She said she planned to tell me the cleaner made a mistake because she knew I'd say no if she'd asked first.

I told her, You didn't ruin my dress by accident. You redesigned it without asking. Then I sent her the receipt for what it would cost to recreate the original handwork. She paid it three days later. We haven't exchanged clothes since.
winners.title: She Borrowed My Dress and Cut Eight Inches Off It
winners.description: She borrowed my favorite custom-made dress for one dinner. It came back permanently altered, and the receipt left in the pocket explained exactly why.
winners.payoff: You didn't ruin my dress by accident. You redesigned it without asking.
